title: Cascaded Tanks Benchmark Combining Soft and Hard Nonlinearities

authors.note: the repository metadata and the PDF spell the second author differently; both are recorded as found

acquisition_context: downloaded by comparison/empirical/fetch-cascaded-tanks.ts from the 4TU.ResearchData file URLs listed by the repository API; publisher MD5 and size verified for each file

source_files.role: documentation (identical to the copy inside the archive)
same data in MATLAB format; not used

measurement_apparatus: two cascaded tanks with free outlets fed by a pump; water level measured with capacitive water level sensors, which are not calibrated, are considered part of the system and can introduce extra nonlinear behaviour; controlled from a Matlab interface to A/D and D/A converters attached to the level sensor and the pump actuator (TanksBenchmark.pdf §2–3)
tank_configuration: upper tank fed by the pump from a reservoir; upper tank drains through a small opening into the lower tank; lower tank drains through a small opening back into the reservoir; on overflow of the upper tank part of the water goes into the lower tank and the rest directly into the reservoir (§2)
measured_variables: water level of the lower tank (output y)
control_inputs: multisine input signals, 1024 points, exciting 0 to 0.0144 Hz, lower frequencies with higher amplitude, zeroth-order hold (§3)
outputs: one output: lower-tank water level (§2, Figure 1 caption)

units.y: V (sensor output; Figure 2 axis 'magnitude (V)'; the sensor is not calibrated, so no level unit is documented)

sampling_regime: uniform sampling, Ts = 4 s (§3; also the Ts column of dataBenchmark.csv)
timebase: sample index 1…1024 at Ts = 4 s; absolute start times not documented in supplied source
number_of_samples: 1024 per record (documented §3; verified: 1024 complete rows in dataBenchmark.csv plus one empty trailing line)
number_of_experiments: 2 records: estimation (columns uEst, yEst) and test (columns uVal, yVal; the file labels the test record 'Val', the documentation calls it the test data)
experiment_duration: 4096 s per record (derived: 1024 × 4 s; not stated separately in the source)
actuator_type: water pump driven by a voltage input; pump model not documented in supplied source
known_nonlinearities: weakly nonlinear outflow relations (square-root law in equations 1–2); hard saturation from overflow of the upper tank and, with a delay, the lower tank; overflow partly stochastic, acting as input-dependent process noise; possible sensor nonlinearity (§2–3, §5)
physical_constraints: tank capacity (overflow); numerical tank heights not documented in supplied source
initial_conditions: system not in steady state during the measurements; states have an unknown initial value, the same for the estimation and the test record (§3)
missingness: none: all four signal columns complete for 1024 rows; the Ts column is filled only in the first row; one empty trailing line

preprocessing.by_this_project: CSV parsed; trailing empty line and the Ts column discarded; no filtering, resampling, detrending or normalization of the stored signals

uncertainty: measured output signal-to-noise ratio close to 40 dB (§3); overflow acts as input-dependent process noise (§2)
intervention_record: the recorded input u is a designed excitation (multisine), not a randomized intervention; there are no recorded outcomes for altered inputs, so counterfactual predictions cannot be checked against data
known_biases: short estimation record; uncalibrated sensors; unknown initial state; single physical setup; stochastic overflow
recommended_split: estimate on the estimation record; the test data should not be used for any purpose during estimation (§4)
benchmark_tasks: report e_RMSt = sqrt(1/N_t Σ (y_mod − y_t)²) on the test record, stating whether y_mod is obtained by simulation (test input only) or prediction (test input and past test outputs); both if the model allows (§4). Note: the printed formula has 1/N_v under the root and defines N_t as the number of test points; this project uses N_t = 1024.
benchmark_challenges: hard saturation with weakly nonlinear normal operation; overflow with input-dependent process noise; short estimation record; unknown initial states (§5)

transformation_history.output: in-memory arrays uEst, yEst, uVal, yVal (1024 each); no file written

redistribution: raw and derived files are not committed; comparison/empirical/fetch-cascaded-tanks.ts reproduces the acquisition and verifies hashes
